Danielle M: Quick sync — I'm trying a credit-smoothing approach in the continuous batcher to reduce starvation for short-sequence tenants. Prototype uses a decaying token-credit bucket + percentile-based refill so long requests don't permanently hog the queue. Thoughts?

Ryan C: Can you sketch the refill rule? is this per-tenant or per-lane?

Danielle M: Per-tenant primary, per-lane fallback. Current pseudo:

```
# every X ms
for tenant in tenants:
  target = max(min_target, p50_token_rate(tenant) * smoothing_factor)
  tenant.credits = lerp(tenant.credits, target, alpha)
```

Where p50_token_rate is a 50th-percentile observed tokens/sec over a sliding window. alpha=0.2 for gentle moves.

Priyanka S: hmm p50 is interesting, reduces influence of rare large bursts. Did you check KV-cache hit-rate correlation? Long sequences often keep KV cache pinned and short ones get cold miss penalty.

Danielle M: Good point. I ran a 2hr perf trace on the staging cluster: tenants that skew long had KV hit rate ~0.92, short-heavy tenants ~0.46 when colocated. When I applied tenant credit smoothing, end-to-end P50 latency for short tenants dropped 28%.

Ryan C: Nice. Do you have the flamegraph / kernel selection impact? Long batches can push the runtime toward fp16-favoring kernels vs int8 fast paths.

Danielle M: Attach: staging-flame-2026-12-03.log (link: https://internal/redwood/perf/staging/179345) — short summary: kernel switch events correlated with queue depth spikes. When a long request enters, the batcher forms a mixed batch and the kernel selector chooses the slower generic attention kernel for safety, increasing overall token latency by ~15% for that mini-batch.

Alvaro G: That's the nasty part — kernel selection is sticky per-batch. Two ideas: 1) prefer homogeneous minibatches by deferring a long request up to T_defer ms if there are short requests queued (bounded wait), or 2) If mixed, prefer a cached quantized variant of the model for the longer sequences to avoid kernel drop. Both have tradeoffs.

Priyanka S: For (1) we risk extra latency for long requests; for SLOs we could make it tenant-tier aware: enterprise tenants get priority to avoid added latency. Also: adjust KV cache eviction to be probability-weighted by tenant credits so short tenants keep a small working set even under pressure.

Ryan C: Can we simulate this with the profiler? I can run a batcher sim: synthetic trace with long/short ratio sweep and measure kernel-choice frequency + KV hit deltas. If we can show solid improvement w/o breaking enterprise SLOs, 👍.

Danielle M: I kicked off a sim run (infra-bot: test-run 1793456789). Basic config: 70% short (<=64 tokens), 30% long (>1024), credits smoothing on vs off. Initial results: smoothing reduces mixed-batch frequency by 41% and short-tenant P95 tail by 18%, overall throughput steady.

infra-bot: test-run 1793456789 started on cluster-staging-3 (cfg: smooth_alpha=0.2, pctl=50, defer_ms=15).

Alvaro G: 15ms defer seems safe. Might need adaptive defer: scale with current queue depth to avoid head-of-line blocking. Also we should update the kernel selector heuristic to add a "fragile-mix" flag: if mixed and variety exceeds X, prefer quantized fallback.

Priyanka S: Another guard: token-budget floor per-tenant so long requests can't drive credits negative. If they drain below floor, we mark them "throttled-long" and route to a preemptible pool with looser SLO but cheaper kernels. This keeps main pool fair.

Danielle M: Love the preemptible pool idea. Implementation plan proposal:
- Phase 1: smoothing + p50 targets + per-tenant credit floor (staging sim).
- Phase 2: adaptive defer_ms + queue-depth scaling + kernel-selector flag (canary on small fleet).
- Phase 3: preemptible pool + KV eviction weighting by credits (enterprise opt-in).

Ryan C: I'll run the full synthetic sweep and push metrics to the perf dashboard. If sims hold, let's run a canary on 2 Dedicated nodes next week.

deploy-bot: canary deploy queued: canary/smooth-credits-v1 -> 2 nodes. ETA 2026-12-04 09:15 UTC.

Danielle M: Action items: Ryan -> full sim + dashboard links, Alvaro -> kernel-selector fragility flag PR, Priyanka -> perf tests for KV eviction weighting, I'll wire the floor and smoothing metric exports. I'll open a short RFC with numbers. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

Ryan C: noted. will post results in this thread when done.

Priyanka S: sgtm.

Alvaro G: will draft kernel-selector change tomorrow.

Danielle M: Closing for now — will update with RFC link.
